key_insight: PEA spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ perovskites under ambient light and thermal stress.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to assess degradation.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite sharing organic-component loss and decomposition into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or operational lifetime; the stability–performance balance remains unresolved.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
